subject: Hosted latency commitments — Pelago: ops runbook & measurement windows
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@pelago.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pelago Procurement <procurement@pelago.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pelago: hosted latency targets and measurement approach

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Pelago is excited about the throughput and prefix-caching you showed. Before we move to an addendum, procurement asked for tighter language on latency commitments and what evidence we would need if we request an exception (e.g., during a major dataset migration or a region failover). A few concrete questions:

- What explicit p50 / p95 targets would Redwood sign up to for the hosted API for our account (US region)?
- How do you define the measurement window (sampling cadence, aggregation epoch)? We need to know how short bursts vs sustained degradation are treated.
- If we request temporary relief / carveouts, what evidence does Redwood accept (traces, token-level logs, KV cache metrics)?
- How do fallbacks to smaller model variants affect commitments? Will requests routed to a fallback be counted against the same SLO?

Can you put together a short ops runbook + evidence checklist we can attach to the SOW? Procurement is aiming to finish legal review by Feb 28, so any guidance this week would be helpful.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30 min call if it’s easier.

Jordan
Director of Platform Engineering
Pelago Analytics
---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@pelago.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Pelago Procurement <procurement@pelago.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pelago: hosted latency targets and measurement approach

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear set of asks. Below is a concise proposal and the attachments referenced (runbook + evidence checklist). I’ve kept the language operational so it can map directly into an SLO addendum. High level: Redwood is comfortable committing to region-scoped SLOs with explicit measurement rules and a defined exception evidence set.

Proposed commitments (US-hosted API, production keys):
- p50: 75 ms end-to-end server-side latency (measured at Redwood ingress)
- p95: 320 ms end-to-end server-side latency
- Availability: 99.95% monthly (non-overlapping maintenance windows apply)

Measurement model (non-ambiguous):
- Sampling: per-request server-side timestamping at ingress and egress; each request is a sample.
- Aggregation: rolling 15-minute windows sampled every minute; for contractual reporting we compute hourly epochs by taking the union of rolling windows and reporting the epoch p50/p95 as the percentile over all samples in that epoch.
- Burst handling: isolated spikes shorter than 2 minutes are treated as transient noise and do not qualify as a sustained SLO breach unless they cause epoch-level p95 to exceed the commitment.
- Deploy carveouts: automated 30-minute carveout per authorized deployment (not cumulative) when Redwood signals maintenance; additional manual carveouts require evidence and prior approval.

Exception evidence (accepted artifacts):
- Token-level latency traces (Redwood-hosted trace ids) for the impacted epoch
- KV cache hit/miss summary for the request distribution during the epoch
- Control-plane events (deploy/restart/scale) with timestamps
- Sampling exports (CSV) for the epoch aligned to UTC

Fallbacks and routing behavior:
- If Redwood routes requests to a documented fallback model variant (e.g., quantized smaller model) due to capacity, we will mark those samples with a model_variant tag. SLOs are measured per-region per-key; fallbacks are included in the primary SLO unless Pelago requests (and we agree in writing) a separate degradation profile for a specific route.

Next steps / action items:
1) I attached a short ops runbook and an evidence checklist (pdf/xlsx) you can attach to the SOW.
2) Ben (cc’d) will scope any changes to our monitoring export contract if Pelago needs longer retention for audits.
3) If Pelago agrees, we’ll generate a DocuSign addendum with the exact epoch language for signature.

I’m free for a 30 min call on Monday to walk through this and confirm wording for the SOW.

—Vivek
VP, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachments: pelago-slo-runbook-v1.pdf, pelago-evidence-checklist.xlsx

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@pelago.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pelago Procurement <procurement@pelago.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pelago: hosted latency targets and measurement approach

Thanks Vivek — helpful and clear. A couple quick clarifications before procurement drafts the addendum:

- Can you confirm the clock sync requirements for server-side timestamping (NTP offset tolerance we should assume)?
- For the 2-minute transient threshold, does that apply per-route or globally across Pelago traffic?

We’d also like to see a short sample trace (token-level) for a 1-hour epoch so our SREs can validate the evidence extraction process. If you can share an anonymized export or a synthetic example, that will speed review.

If Monday works for you, let’s take the 30 min to walk through it; procurement wants to capture the carveout language precisely.

Jordan
---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@pelago.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Pelago Procurement <procurement@pelago.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 16:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pelago: hosted latency targets and measurement approach

Jordan — quick answers and artifacts attached.

- Clock sync: Redwood requires ingress/egress hosts to be within 200 ms of UTC (we use leap-aware NTP state; we’ll include the timestamp offsets in the exported trace csv). That tolerance is already reflected in our monitoring parsers and is contract-ready.
- 2-minute transient threshold: applied per-route (route = API key + model_variant + region). If multiple routes spike simultaneously we will analyze on a per-route basis and then reconcile at epoch aggregation time.

Attached is a sanitized 1-hour synthetic trace demonstrating token-level export fields (trace_id, model_variant, kv_hit, token_latency_ms, request_timestamp). Ben will follow up on retention options for forensic exports (cc).

I’ll send a calendar invite for Monday 10:30 PT and a DocuSign link for the addendum draft; procurement can sign after the call if the language is acceptable.

—Vivek
VP, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachments: pelago-slo-runbook-v1.pdf, pelago-evidence-checklist.xlsx
